messages:
Alex: taking over primary for the 20:00->04:00 window :wave:  quick context — P310 (inference latency spike) is still active; main mitigation is prefix cache warmup. i'm going to swap driving with Maria in ~10m. leaving current checklist below.

Oncall Bot: INCIDENT P310 triggered - page sent to #eng-oncall - severity: 2 - affected: hosted text-gen endpoints - runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/p310-latency

Maria: ok i'm ready to take the driver role at T+10. main visible symptom is 95th latency hitting ~6s for long-context requests. small % of customer requests time out.

Alex: copy. planning to handoff driver -> Maria, comms ownership needed. Kevin, can you own comms and customer updates for the next 90m? you'll have read-only access to the incident doc in Confluence. @Kevin? :eyes:

Kevin: i can take comms for first hour, then Jess can pick up if still hot. will post an update to the incident channel and start a short status note for CS.

Jess: happy to jump in after Kevin. note: we have a coverage gap 02:00-03:00 UTC where no dedicated comms is scheduled — Samir, can you stand by as fallback?

Samir: can stand by but not primary — i'll triage alerts if they escalate to P1.

Alex: thanks. quick technical pointers for whoever is driving:
- check prefix cache hit rate: `curl -s https://metrics.internal/api?m=prefix_cache_hit`
- if hit rate < 75% restart the cache-populator pod: `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/cache-populator`
- watch cpu/gpu utilization on serving nodes: `grafana -> Redwood / Serving / Node Utilization`

Maria: also note that autoscaler has been oscillating. temp mitigations: reduce batch size to 8 on the g4 pools and enable cache-only routing for critical tenants.

Alex: putting the exact commands here in case you need them quickly:
```bash
# reduce batch size for g4 pool
redwoodctl pools update g4 --batch-size 8
# enable cache-only route for tenant 'acme'
redwoodctl routing set --tenant acme --policy cache-first
```

Maria: ran the autoscaler health check. logs show frequent OOMs in `inference-worker` around 19:42 which correlates with the 95th spike. attaching last 20 lines:
```
[19:42:11] inference-worker[pid=3421]: OOMKilled at 0x7ff12...
[19:42:12] inference-worker[pid=3421]: restarting process
[19:42:13] autoscaler: scale-down deferred due to bucketed load
```

Kevin: will post public-facing status: "We’re investigating elevated generation latencies affecting a subset of requests. Engineers are actively mitigating; next update in 30m." :writing_hand:

Alex: decision log: driver = Maria, comms = Kevin (Jess backup at +60m, Samir fallback overnight). i'll transfer pager and bridge host to Maria in 10m.

Maria: taking driver now. starting the cache-populator restart and lowering batch size to 8. i’ll report back with metrics in ~8m. :thumbsup:

Oncall Bot: bridge created: https://meetings.internal/bridge/2154326789 - added participants: Alex, Maria, Kevin, Jess, Samir

Maria: quick metrics after changes — prefix cache hit -> 82%, 95th latency -> 3.2s (was 6s). no new OOMs observed in last 5m. seems improvement but monitoring for regression.

Kevin: posted update to incident doc and pinged CS. customers flagged: acme-enterprise (partial timeouts), beta-team (degraded throughput).

Alex: nice. next steps: hold on-nightwatch handover plan. Maria, if you need to escalate to infra please tag `@oncall-sre` and escalate to P1 if errors > 5% over 15m.

Maria: noted. leaving detailed checklist in the incident doc and tagging alerts for Samir to be ready at 02:00 UTC. handing pager to Maria now.

Alex: handing off fully — i'm available for context but dropping out as primary. thanks team. :raised_hands:
